idiom_name: frozen dataclass snapshots + bisect over a sorted history list (bisect_right with key=)
implementation_notes: The version is a frozen dataclass (or NamedTuple) - frozen=True stops assignment to the snapshot itself - and the continuity keeps a plain list of versions sorted by effective date; bisect.bisect_right(history, on, key=...) returns the insertion point after all versions effective on or before the query date, so history[i - 1] is the version in force and i == 0 is the 'no version yet' case. That is the whole temporal collection; the update path is dataclasses.replace(current, ...) for a working copy plus bisect.insort to add it at its effective date. Third-party time libraries (arrow, pendulum) change the date type, not the structure.
pitfalls: frozen=True is shallow: a dict or list field can still be mutated in place, so a published version changes retroactively - use tuples/frozen values or copy in __post_init__.
bisect assumes the list is sorted, so appending a retroactive amendment corrupts every later lookup (use insort); the key= parameter also requires Python 3.10+.
Mixing date and datetime keys, or naive and aware datetimes, raises TypeError or orders silently wrong - pick one key type at the boundary.
bisect_right vs bisect_left is the boundary rule: bisect_right makes a version effective on the query date the one in force, while bisect_left would keep the earlier version for that whole day.
